shared_elements: low-relief carving on a large upright stone block
curved crescent/arc form near the top
field of short parallel incised lines (comb- or rib-like hatching)
curvilinear animal-like body with a tapering limb or tail
weathered, monochrome stone surface photographed outdoors in situ
justification: Both show shallow, rounded relief on a monumental weathered stone, and each includes a crescent/arc paired with a disc and a patch of short parallel incised strokes below it, which is the most specific echo. But A is organised into stacked horizontal registers of legible animal and human figures with a banded zigzag frieze, whereas B carries a single large, ambiguous curvilinear motif spread over an irregular boulder, and the carving technique (crisp, controlled outlines versus broad, eroded grooves) differs markedly.
